chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Munqari, from Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Luqman said to his son: When you travel with a group, frequently consult them regarding your affairs and their affairs, and smile often in their faces, and be generous with your provisions. And if they call you, respond to them, and if they seek your help, assist them. And surpass them in three qualities: length of silence, abundance of prayer, and generosity of the self with whatever you have of an animal, wealth, or provisions.

And if they ask you to testify to the truth, testify for them, and strive with your opinion for them when they consult you. Then do not finalize your advice until you are certain and consider it, and do not answer in consultation until you stand regarding it, sit, sleep, eat, and pray, while utilizing your thought and wisdom in your advice. For whoever does not refine his sincerity for the one who consulted him, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will strip him of his opinion and remove trustworthiness from him.

And when you see your companions walking, walk with them, and when you see them working, work with them, and when they give charity and give a loan, give with them. And listen to the one who is older than you in age, and if they order you with a matter and ask you, say 'Yes' and do not say 'No', for 'No' is a fault and blame. And if you are confused in your path, dismount, and if you doubt the direction, stop and consult one another.

And when you see a single person, do not ask him about your path nor seek his guidance, for the single person in the wilderness is suspect; perhaps he is an eye for the thieves, or he is the Satan who confused you. And beware of two persons as well, unless you see what I do not see, for the intellectual, when he sees something with his own eyes, recognizes the truth from it, and the witness sees what the absent one does not.

O my son! When the time for prayer comes, do not delay it for anything, and pray it and rest from it, for it is a debt. And pray in congregation even if it is on the head of a camel, and do not sleep on your animal, for that is quick to affect its back, and that is not from the action of the wise unless you are in a carriage where you can stretch to relax your joints.

And when you near the destination, dismount from your animal and begin by feeding it before yourself. And when you intend to encamp, choose from the lands the best in color, softest in soil, and most abundant in grass. And when you settle, pray two cycles before you sit. And when you intend to fulfill your need, go far away in the land. And when you embark, pray two cycles, and bid farewell to the land you stayed in, and send greetings upon it and upon its people, for every patch of land has its inhabitants from the angels.

And if you can, do not eat food until you begin by giving charity from it, so do so. And upon you is to recite the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as long as you are riding. And upon you is glorification as long as you are working. And upon you is supplication as long as you are alone. And beware of traveling from the beginning of the night. And upon you is to stay overnight and travel from the middle of the night to its end. And beware of raising your voice during your travel.

key_terms.الدَّلْجَة: Traveling in the latter part of the night

ai.seo_question: What are the ethical and practical guidelines for travel in Shia hadith according to Luqman?
ai.summary: This hadith, often cited as the 'Hadith of Islam' in al-Kafi, presents Luqman’s advice as a comprehensive manual for social and spiritual conduct during travel, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating ritual piety with practical wisdom. It highlights the virtue of *shura* (consultation) and *sakhā’* (generosity) as means to earn divine favor and maintain communal harmony, while offering specific jurisprudential details on prayer timing and animal care. The text underscores the concept that proper etiquette is a form of worship, linking physical actions like feeding beasts and greeting angels to spiritual integrity.

en.hubeali: H 14994 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood Al-Munqary, from Hammaad, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said;

‘Luqman<sup>as</sup> said to his<sup>as</sup> son: ‘Whenever you travel with a group, take a lot of advice about them for your affairs and their affairs, and smile frequently in their faces, and be generous with your provisions. And if they call you, respond to them, and if they seek your support, help them. And be overcome them with three things – the length of silence, and the frequency of the Prayer, and generosity of the self with whatever is with you from the animal, or wealth, or provisions.

And if they ask you to testify to ‘الْحَقِّ’ the truth, so testify for it, and exhaust your opinion for them if they consult you. Then do not advise them until you are sure about it and reconsider it, and do not answer in your advice until you stand regarding it, and sit, and sleep, and eat, and Pray, and you are utilising your thoughts and your wisdom with regards to your advice. So the one who does not refine his advice for the one who consulted him, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Crucifies his opinion, and Removes from him the trust.

And if you see your companions walking, so you should walk with them, and if you see them doing something, so do it with them, and if they give charity and give a loan, so give with them. And listen to the one who is older than you in age, and if he orders you and asks you, so say, Yes’, and do not say, ‘No’, for the ‘No’ is a fault and blameable. And if you are confused regarding your road, so stop and encamp, and if you are in doubt regarding the intended course, pause and plan.

And if you see one person, do not ask him about your direction of road, and do not heed his guidance, for the one person in the wild is suspect for he could be an eye for the thieves, or he could be the Satan<sup>la</sup> who confused you. And be cautious of two persons as well, unless you can see what I<sup>as</sup> don’t, for the intellectual, when he sees something with his own eyes recognises the truth from it, and the witness can see what the absentee does not.

O my son! And when the time of Salat comes up, so do not delay it for anything, and offer Salat and seek comfort from it for it is the Religion. And Pray in congregation even if there is pushing upon the head. And do not sleep upon your animal for that is injurious to its back, and that is not from the actions of the wise except if you are in a carriage and it is possible for you to stretch your joints.

And when you come close to the destination, so descend from your animal and begin by feeding it before yourself. And when you intend to encamp, so it is upon you to remain in a land, which is good in colour, soft in soil, and abundance of grass. And if you encamp, so Pray two cycles before you sit down. And if you intend to fulfill your need (toilet), go far away. And when you embark (upon your journey) Pray two cycles, and say farewell to the land on which you spent time, and send greetings of peace upon it and upon its people, because for every patch of land has its inhabitants from the Angels.

If you are able to, do not eat food until you begin by giving charity from it, so do it. And it is upon you to recite the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic as long as you are riding. And it is upon you for the Glorification for as long as you are working. And it is upon you to supplicate for as long as you are alone. And beware of travelling in the first part of the night. And it is upon you to travel from the middle of the night to its end. And beware of raising your voice during your travel’.
en.sarwar: 548. A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al-Husayn Bin Yazeed Al-Nowfaly, from Ali Bin Dawood Al-Yaqouby, from Isa Bin Abdullah Al-Alawy who said: It has been narrated to me by Al-Asaydi and Muhammad Bin Basheer that Abdullah Bin Naf’a Al-Azraq used to say, ‘If only I knew someone between its (earth’s) diameter where my animal (ride) can reach to, who can debate with me that Ali (a.s.) killed the people of Naharwaan, and he (a.s.) was not unjust to them, I would ride over to him’ (to refute). So it was said to him, ‘And (what about his (a.s.) son (a.s.))?’ He said, ‘Is his (a.s.) son (a.s.) a knowledgeable one?’ So it was said to him, ‘This is your first ignorance. And have they (a.s.) ever been without a knowledgeable one?’ He said, ‘So who is their (a.s.) knowledgeable one today?’ It was said, ‘Muhammad (a.s.) Bin Ali (a.s.) Bin Al-Husayn Bin Ali (a.s.)’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he rode over to him (a.s.) with the brave ones of his companions until he came up to Al-Medina. So he sought permission to see Abu Ja’far (a.s.). It was said to him (a.s.), ‘This is Abdullah Bin Naf’a’. He (a.s.) said; ‘So what has he to do with me (a.s.), and he ‘يَبْرَأُ’ distances himself (Tabarra) from me (a.s.) and from my (a.s.) father (a.s.) both morning and evening’. Abu Baseer Al-Kufy said to him (a.s.), ‘May I be sacrificed for you (a.s.), this one alleges that, ‘‘If only I knew someone between its (earth’s) diameter where my animal (ride) can reach to, who can debate with me that Ali (a.s.) killed the people of Naharwaan, and he (a.s.) was not unjust to them, I would ride over to him (to refute)’. So Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to him: ‘You think he has come to me (a.s.) for a debate?’ He said, ‘Yes’. He (a.s.) said: ‘O boy (servant), go out and unload his saddlebag, and tell him to come to us (a.s.) tomorrow’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So when it was the next day, Abdullah Bin Naf’a came with the brave ones of his companions, and Abu Ja’far (a.s.) sent a message to all the sons of the Emigrants and the Helpers and gathered them. Then he (a.s.) came out to the people wearing two alluring robes and faced the people as if he (a.s.) was the moon in orbit. So he (a.s.) said: ‘The Praise is due to Allah (azwj), the Awarder of the positions, and the Attribute of the attributes, and the Director of the directions. The Praise is due to Allah (azwj) “[2:255] slumber does not overtake Him nor sleep; whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth is His” up to the end of the Verse. ‘And I (a.s.) testify that there is no god except for Allah (azwj), One, with no associates to Him (azwj). And I (a.s.) testify that Muhammad (saww) is His (azwj) servant, Chosen by Him (azwj) and Guided by Him (azwj) to be on the Straight Path. The Praise is due to Allah (azwj) Who Honoured us (a.s.) with the Prophet-hood and Favoured us by Al-Wilayah. O group of the sons of the Emigrants and the Helpers! The ones among you who have merits regarding Ali (a.s.) Bin Abu Talib (a.s.), so he should stand and narrate them’. So the people stood up, so they enumerated those merits. Abdullah said, ‘I am a narrator of these merits from them, but, subsequently the disbelief took place after the appointment of the two judges’. Then they ended up with the merits in the Hadeeth of Khyber: ‘I (saww) shall give the flag tomorrow to a man who loves Allah (azwj) and His (azwj) Messenger (saww), and Allah (azwj) and His (azwj) Messenger (saww) love him (a.s.). An attacking one, not a fleeing one who will not return until Allah (azwj) Grants victory upon his (a.s.) hands’. So Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said; ‘What do you say regarding this Hadeeth’. He said, ‘True. There is no doubt with regards to it, but disbelief took place afterwards’. So Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to him: ‘May your mother be bereft of you! Inform me (a.s.) about Allah (azwj) Loving Ali (a.s.) Bin Abu Talib (a.s.) on the Day He (azwj) Loved him (a.s.) and He (azwj) Knew that he (a.s.) would be killing the people of Nahrwan, or did He (azwj) not Know?’ Ibn Naf’a said, ‘Repeat that for me’. So Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to him: ‘Inform me (a.s.) about Allah (azwj), He (azwj) Loved Ali (a.s.) on the day that He (azwj) Loved him (a.s.), and He (azwj) Knew that he (a.s.) would be killing the people of Nahrwan, or did He (azwj) not Know?’ He said, ‘If I say, ‘No’, I would have blasphemed’. He (the narrator) said, ‘So he said, ‘He (azwj) had Known’. He (a.s.) said: ‘So did Allah (azwj) Love Ali (a.s.) to act in obedience to Him (azwj) or in disobedience to Him (azwj)?’ He (a.s.) said; ‘Upon his (a.s.) acting in obedience to Him (azwj)’. So Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to him: ‘So stand up (and leave) for you have been defeated’.
He stood up and he was saying, ‘Until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread at dawn, Allah (azwj) Knows where He (azwj) should Make His (azwj) Message to be’.
